model_annotation: Figure 4, titled “Number of participants (N = 6) who highlighted each evaluation criterion as beneficial,” is a horizontal bar chart that visually represents the frequency with which six participants identified specific features of the developed fact-checking tool as beneficial. The vertical axis lists six evaluation criteria: “Retrieval of relevant FCs,” “Concise summaries,” “Clarity of interface,” “Explanations,” “Veracity graph,” and “Overall usability.” The horizontal axis represents the count of participants, ranging from 0 to 6, with tick marks at integer intervals. Each criterion is associated with a single horizontal bar, colored in a uniform dark gray, whose length corresponds to the number of participants who selected that criterion. The bar for “Retrieval of relevant FCs” extends to 6, indicating all participants found this beneficial. “Concise summaries” and “Clarity of interface” both reach 5 participants. “Explanations” and “Veracity graph” are each selected by 4 participants. “Overall usability” is rated beneficial by 3 participants. The bars are arranged in descending order of participant count from top to bottom, visually emphasizing the most highly valued features. No legend or additional annotations are present, and the chart is embedded within the text of Section 8.2, which discusses user study results.
